# Friday Works video editor: command interface for AI agents

> A video editor that runs in the browser, on phones and computers, made by Friday Works from OpenCut (MIT). Besides its touch interface it has a text command interface for AI agents, which can make a whole video with it: import clips, cut and arrange them, add text, captions, stickers, effects, masks and animation, check frames, and export an MP4. Nothing is uploaded: media stay in the visitor's browser and the export downloads to their device.

## Where it is

- The editor: https://nguyenxvotanminh3.github.io/fridayworks-hosted-apps/video/ (add ?lang=vi for a Vietnamese interface). On fridayweworks.com it is embedded at https://fridayweworks.com/vi/tools/dung-video and https://fridayweworks.com/en/tools/video-editor.
- Console: open https://nguyenxvotanminh3.github.io/fridayworks-hosted-apps/video/?ai=1 (or ?lang=vi&ai=1). A panel named "AI command console" appears beside the editor (below it on phones). Type commands in its "Command" box and press Enter; each command, its output and its JSON data appear in the "Command results" log.
- JavaScript: `await window.fridayworksAI.run("state")` runs one or more command lines and resolves with one result per line: `{ ok, command, output, data, error, hint }`. `window.fridayworksAI.help()` and `window.fridayworksAI.commands()` describe every command.
- WebMCP: in browsers that support WebMCP, the page registers one tool per command (video_state, video_text_add, video_export, …) plus video_run_script.

## How to work

1. Run `state` to see the project: frame size, ratio, duration, media, and every element by track with its #n and id.
2. Bring in media with `media import <url>` (the URL must allow cross-origin requests; data: URLs always work), or upload a file from the device with the page's file input ("Add media" / "Thêm video").
3. Build the video with `project ratio`, `text add`, `captions generate` or `captions import`, `sticker add`, `element set`, `element timing`, `element trim`, `element split`, `effect add`, `mask add`, `keyframe add` and `speed`.
4. Look at the result with `snapshot --at <seconds>` (a PNG data URL in data.png) and fix what looks wrong.
5. Run `export` (or `export --preset tiktok`). The MP4 downloads to the user's device.

Rules of thumb:
- Times are in seconds ("2.5", "0:02.5"). Elements are referred to by #n from `state`, by id or id prefix, or as `last` (the element added last) or `selected`. Numbers change after deletions, so run `state` again.
- Text does not wrap by itself: put \n inside the quotes where a line should break, then check with `snapshot`.
- One command per line; "; " (a semicolon and a space) also separates commands, while a semicolon inside a value such as data:video/mp4;base64,… does not.
- Every error says what was wrong and usually how to fix it (a "hint"). `undo` reverts the last change.
- `captions generate` downloads a speech model the first time (about 150 MB) and can take minutes. `captions import` with SRT text is instant.

## Commands

### Basics

```
help [<command>] [--json]
  Lists the commands, or explains one. --json gives every command with its arguments as JSON.
  <command>        A command name, e.g. "text add".
  --json           Return the full command list as JSON data.
  Examples:
    help
    help text add
    help --json
```

```
state
  Describes the project: size, ratio, fps, background, duration, playhead, media, and every element by track (top layer first) with its #n, id, type, times and text.
  Examples:
    state
```

```
snapshot [--at <seconds>] [--max <number>]
  Renders the frame at a time as a PNG (data.png is a data: URL) so you can check the layout. Moves the playhead there.
  --at             Time to render. (default: the playhead)
  --max            Longest side of the image in pixels. (default: 640)
  Examples:
    snapshot --at 2
    snapshot --at 0 --max 1080
```

### Project

```
project ratio <ratio>
  Sets the frame to a preset size: 9:16 is 1080×1920 (TikTok, Reels, Shorts), 16:9 is 1920×1080 (YouTube), 1:1 is 1080×1080, 4:3 is 1440×1080. Elements keep their positions.
  <ratio>          The aspect ratio. (one of 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:3)
  Examples:
    project ratio 9:16
```

```
project size <width> <height>
  Sets a custom frame size in pixels.
  <width>          Width in pixels.
  <height>         Height in pixels.
  Examples:
    project size 1080 1350
```

```
project fps <fps>
  Sets the frame rate.
  <fps>            Frames per second. (one of 24, 25, 30, 60, 120)
  Examples:
    project fps 30
```

```
project background [--color <color>] [--blur <light|medium|heavy>]
  Sets what shows behind the clips: a colour, or a blurred copy of the main clip.
  --color          A colour such as #000000 or white.
  --blur           Blur the main clip behind itself instead. (one of light, medium, heavy)
  Examples:
    project background --color #101820
    project background --blur medium
```

```
project rename <name>
  Renames the project. The exported file takes this name.
  <name>           The new name.
  Examples:
    project rename "Ra mắt sản phẩm"
```

### Media

```
media import <url> [--name <string>] [--start <seconds>] [--timeline]
  Downloads a video, image or audio file into the project and puts it on the timeline (videos and images after the last clip, audio at the playhead). The URL must allow cross-origin requests (CORS); data: URLs always work. For a file on the user's device, upload it with the page's file input ("Add media" / "Thêm video") instead.
  <url>            https:// or data: URL of the file.
  --name           File name to use, with its extension. (default: from the URL)
  --start          Put it at this time instead.
  --timeline       Put it on the timeline; --no-timeline only adds it to the media list. (default: true)
  Examples:
    media import https://example.com/clip.mp4
    media import https://example.com/song.mp3 --start 0
    media import https://example.com/logo.png --no-timeline
```

```
media list
  Lists the imported files with their ids, types, durations and sizes.
  Examples:
    media list
```

```
media add <asset> [--start <seconds>]
  Puts an imported file on the timeline (again).
  <asset>          The media id or id prefix from "media list".
  --start          Timeline time it starts at, in seconds. (default: the playhead)
  Examples:
    media add 3f9a --start 6
```

### Text

```
text add <content> [--start <seconds>] [--duration <seconds>] [--look <outline|yellow|box|large|soft|plain>] [--size <number>] [--font <string>] [--color <color>] [--bold] [--italic] [--align <left|center|right>] [--place <top|middle|bottom>] [--x <number>] [--y <number>] [--outline <color>] [--shadow <color>] [--box <color>]
  Adds a text element. Use \n inside quotes for a new line. Font size is in editor units (5 is subtitle size, 15 is a title on a landscape frame).
  <content>        The text.
  --start          Timeline time it starts at, in seconds. (default: the playhead)
  --duration       How long it lasts, in seconds. (default: 5)
  --look           A ready-made caption look (sets colour, outline, shadow, box and size). (one of outline, yellow, box, large, soft, plain)
  --size           Font size in editor units.
  --font           Font family, e.g. "Be Vietnam Pro" (any Google Font; "fonts" lists the ones with Vietnamese).
  --color          Text colour.
  --bold           Bold text.
  --italic         Italic text.
  --align          Text alignment. (one of left, center, right)
  --place          Vertical place in the frame. (one of top, middle, bottom; default: middle)
  --x              Horizontal offset from the centre, in pixels (+ is right).
  --y              Vertical offset from the centre, in pixels (+ is down). Overrides --place.
  --outline        Outline colour (turns the outline on).
  --shadow         Drop shadow colour (turns the shadow on).
  --box            Background box colour (turns the box on).
  Examples:
    text add "Xin chào!" --start 0 --duration 3 --size 12 --outline black --place top
    text add "Giảm 50%\nHôm nay thôi" --look yellow --place bottom
```

```
fonts [<search>] [--vietnamese]
  Lists font families. --vietnamese keeps only fonts that draw every Vietnamese tone mark.
  <search>         Part of a font name.
  --vietnamese     Only fonts with the Vietnamese subset.
  Examples:
    fonts --vietnamese
    fonts be vietnam
```

### Captions

```
captions generate [--lang <string>] [--model <base|small>] [--look <outline|yellow|box|large|soft|plain>]
  Transcribes the timeline's audio in the browser with Whisper and adds the captions on a new text track. The first run downloads the model (about 150 MB for base, 300 MB for small); it can take minutes. Vietnamese captions are cut by length.
  --lang           Language code such as vi, en, ja, or auto. (default: auto)
  --model          base is faster and lighter, small is more accurate. (one of base, small; default: base)
  --look           Caption look. (one of outline, yellow, box, large, soft, plain; default: outline)
  Examples:
    captions generate --lang vi --look yellow
```

```
captions import <subtitles> [--look <outline|yellow|box|large|soft|plain>]
  Adds captions from SRT or ASS text (or a URL to such a file) on a new text track. SRT takes the look; ASS keeps its own styles.
  <subtitles>      The SRT/ASS text (\n for new lines) or an https:// URL.
  --look           Caption look for SRT. (one of outline, yellow, box, large, soft, plain; default: outline)
  Examples:
    captions import "1\n00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:02,000\nXin chào\n\n2\n00:00:02,000 --> 00:00:04,000\nCảm ơn bạn"
```

```
captions looks
  Lists the ready-made caption looks.
  Examples:
    captions looks
```

### Elements

```
element info <element>
  Shows one element: its timing, and every parameter you can set with "element set", with its current value, type and range.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    element info #1
    element info last
```

```
element set <element> [key=value ...]
  Sets parameters of an element, e.g. position, scale, rotation, opacity, volume (dB), text, font, colours, outline, shadow and box. "element info" lists them. Values are checked and clamped.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  key=value        One or more parameter=value pairs, e.g. opacity=0.5 transform.positionY=600 color=#ffd84d stroke.enabled=true.
  Examples:
    element set #1 opacity=0.8 transform.scaleX=1.2 transform.scaleY=1.2
    element set last content="Xin chào" fontSize=8
    element set #3 volume=-6
```

```
element timing <element> [--start <seconds>] [--duration <seconds>]
  Moves an element and/or changes how long it lasts. For video and audio clips, --duration trims or extends the end (within the source).
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  --start          Timeline time it starts at, in seconds. (default: the playhead)
  --duration       New length in seconds.
  Examples:
    element timing #2 --start 1.5 --duration 4
```

```
element trim <element> [--from <seconds>] [--to <seconds>]
  Chooses which part of a video or audio file the clip plays, in seconds of the source file. The clip keeps its start time.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  --from           Source time the clip begins with. (default: 0)
  --to             Source time the clip ends with. (default: the end of the file)
  Examples:
    element trim #3 --from 2 --to 7.5
```

```
element split <element> --at <seconds>
  Cuts an element in two at a timeline time. The right part becomes "last".
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  --at             Timeline time of the cut.
  Examples:
    element split #3 --at 4
```

```
element duplicate <element>
  Copies an element onto a new track at the same time. The copy becomes "last".
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    element duplicate #1
```

```
element delete <element>
  Deletes an element.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    element delete #4
```

```
element mute <element> [--on]
  Mutes a video or audio clip (--no-on unmutes).
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  --on             Mute (true) or unmute (false). (default: true)
  Examples:
    element mute #3
    element mute #3 --no-on
```

```
element hide <element> [--on]
  Hides a visual element (--no-on shows it again).
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  --on             Hide (true) or show (false). (default: true)
  Examples:
    element hide #2
```

```
element select <element>
  Selects an element in the editor, so "selected" refers to it.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    element select #2
```

```
speed <element> <rate> [--keep-pitch]
  Changes the playback speed of a video or audio clip (0.1 to 5). The clip's length changes with it.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  <rate>           Speed factor: 2 is twice as fast, 0.5 half.
  --keep-pitch     Keep the voice's pitch.
  Examples:
    speed #3 1.5 --keep-pitch
```

### Stickers and shapes

```
sticker add <sticker> [--start <seconds>] [--duration <seconds>]
  Adds a sticker: a flag (flags:VN, flags:US …) or a shape (shapes:rectangle, shapes:ellipse, shapes:polygon, shapes:star). "sticker search" finds ids.
  <sticker>        Sticker id.
  --start          Timeline time it starts at, in seconds. (default: the playhead)
  --duration       How long it lasts, in seconds. (default: 5)
  Examples:
    sticker add flags:VN --start 0 --duration 3
    sticker add shapes:star
```

```
sticker search <query>
  Finds stickers by name (country names work in English or Vietnamese).
  <query>          Search words.
  Examples:
    sticker search viet nam
    sticker search star
```

### Effects and masks

```
effect add <element> <effect> [--intensity <number>]
  Adds an effect to one element. This build has one effect: blur (intensity 0–100).
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  <effect>         The effect. (one of blur)
  --intensity      Effect strength. (default: 15)
  Examples:
    effect add #3 blur --intensity 40
```

```
effect layer <effect> [--start <seconds>] [--duration <seconds>] [--intensity <number>]
  Adds an effect as its own layer, which applies to everything below it for its time span.
  <effect>         The effect. (one of blur)
  --start          Timeline time it starts at, in seconds. (default: the playhead)
  --duration       How long it lasts, in seconds. (default: 5)
  --intensity      Effect strength. (default: 15)
  Examples:
    effect layer blur --start 0 --duration 2 --intensity 60
```

```
effect remove <element>
  Removes all effects from an element.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    effect remove #3
```

```
mask add <element> <shape> [--invert] [--feather <number>]
  Masks a video, image or shape so only part of it shows (one mask per element).
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  <shape>          Mask shape. (one of rectangle, ellipse, heart, diamond, star, split, cinematic-bars)
  --invert         Show the outside instead.
  --feather        Soft edge, 0–100.
  Examples:
    mask add #3 ellipse --feather 20
    mask add #3 cinematic-bars
```

```
mask remove <element>
  Removes the mask of an element.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  Examples:
    mask remove #3
```

### Animation

```
keyframe add <element> <param> --at <seconds> --value <string> [--curve <linear|hold|bezier>]
  Animates a parameter: sets its value at a timeline time. Two keyframes or more make it change smoothly. Works for position, scale, rotation, opacity, colours and volume.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  <param>          Parameter key from "element info", e.g. opacity or transform.scaleX.
  --at             Timeline time, inside the element.
  --value          The value at that time.
  --curve          How it moves to the next keyframe. (one of linear, hold, bezier; default: linear)
  Examples:
    keyframe add #1 opacity --at 0 --value 0
    keyframe add #1 opacity --at 0.5 --value 1
```

```
keyframe remove <element> <param> --at <seconds>
  Removes the keyframe of a parameter at a timeline time.
  <element>        The element: its id, an id prefix, #n from "state", "last" or "selected".
  <param>          Parameter key.
  --at             Timeline time of the keyframe.
  Examples:
    keyframe remove #1 opacity --at 0
```

### Playback and history

```
seek <time>
  Moves the playhead. New text and stickers start at the playhead unless --start is given.
  <time>           Timeline time.
  Examples:
    seek 2.5
```

```
play
  Plays from the playhead (the picture only, unless someone has tapped the page).
  Examples:
    play
```

```
pause
  Pauses playback.
  Examples:
    pause
```

```
undo
  Undoes the last change.
  Examples:
    undo
```

```
redo
  Redoes the last undone change.
  Examples:
    redo
```

### Output

```
export [--format <mp4|webm>] [--quality <low|medium|high|very_high>] [--size <original|1080p>] [--preset <tiktok|youtube>] [--audio] [--download]
  Renders the video and downloads it to the user's device (named after the project). Takes about as long as the video, longer on phones. --preset tiktok frames 9:16, youtube 16:9, both MP4 at most 1080p.
  --format         File format. (one of mp4, webm; default: mp4)
  --quality        Quality. (one of low, medium, high, very_high; default: high)
  --size           Keep the frame size, or cap the short side at 1080. (one of original, 1080p; default: original)
  --preset         One-step framing and settings for a platform. (one of tiktok, youtube)
  --audio          Include sound (--no-audio for a silent video). (default: true)
  --download       Download the file (--no-download only reports its size). (default: true)
  Examples:
    export
    export --preset tiktok
    export --format webm --quality medium --no-audio
```
